purpose: Research-only evidence packet for five individually registered Dublin City NIAH structures in the Connolly Station and Talbot Street area

source_snapshot.queue_rule: Each selected registration number was checked as an exact entry in the workflow-generated Dublin missing-registration queue.

official_dataset_reference.title: NIAH Data Download
official_dataset_reference.note: Official national CSV provides ITM coordinates and latitude/longitude. Individual NIAH page coordinate pairs are preserved separately as raw values because the page does not label their CRS.

candidate_records.name: Sheriff Street Lower railway warehouse
candidate_records.address: North side of Sheriff Street Lower, Dublin 1, Ireland
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010132 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Attached fourteen-bay two-storey former railway building, built c.1850, with upper floor removed, lining the north side of Sheriff Street Lower. NIAH describes random-coursed squared and snecked calp limestone walls, tooled piers and voussoired round arches to the bays. The westernmost four bays retain part of an upper level. The building is now described as a customer car park for Connolly Station. It is a remnant of a railway warehouse and part of the station's wider industrial complex.

candidate_records.name: Bank of Ireland
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010135 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Terraced two-bay three-storey red-brick former house, built c.1860, with a timber shopfront and ATM, currently recorded as a bank. NIAH highlights Flemish-bond brickwork, gauged segmental-headed window openings, timber sliding sash windows, fluted engaged pilasters and scrolled shopfront consoles. The street was laid out following the sale of Tyrone House c.1840.

candidate_records.name: Dublin Electric Theatre
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010136 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Terraced six-bay two-storey red-brick former cinema, built c.1911, designed by George Moore. NIAH records the building as originally two buildings unified by matching fabric, including a flush granite platband and red-brick parapet coping. The shaped Dutch gable and early cinema history make it an important cultural record. The official page describes a shopfront at ground level and the property as vacant at survey time; the CSV queue description records the same former cinema and vacant status. Do not interpret that survey-time status as current.

candidate_records.name: Roasted Bean Coffee Company
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010138 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Terraced two-bay three-storey house, built c.1860, with shopfront to ground floor and recorded in use as a restaurant. NIAH describes a slate roof, rendered parapet, ruled-and-lined render, masonry quoins, moulded architraves and timber sliding sash windows. The timber shopfront has fluted consoles, a fanlighted upper-floor entrance and glazed door. It forms part of the terrace lining the south side of Talbot Street.

candidate_records.name: Scruples
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010139 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Terraced two-bay three-storey house, built c.1860, with a recent rendered shopfront at ground floor. NIAH notes survival of much of the original form and fabric, including timber sash windows, masonry and render embellishments, moulded architraves and pedimented window lintels. It is an integral component of the substantial terrace lining the south side of Talbot Street.

spatial_and_identity_cautions: 50010132 is a former railway warehouse on Sheriff Street Lower and a distinct structure associated with Connolly Station. Do not merge it with the station building, head office or train shed.
50010135, 50010138 and 50010139 are separate registered buildings on Talbot Street. The terrace is a shared streetscape context, not a single building identity.

50010136 is a six-bay former cinema described by NIAH as originally two buildings unified by matching fabric. Retain the single NIAH registration as one archive candidate; do not split the historic cinema into two separate archive records without new footprint-level evidence.
Individual NIAH page coordinate pairs are preserved as raw values because the page does not label their CRS. Do not interpret them as EPSG:2157 or overwrite official CSV coordinates.
NIAH descriptions of use, vacancy, condition and alterations are survey-time source statements, not present-day field verification.
No physical access, ownership, public access or current condition has been verified.
